summary: Uses Digital and IT’s 4 September mature-team estimate as the current high-water funding baseline for the Digital Student Experience Hub, while keeping known existing capacity and unresolved sharing or scope questions explicit so the envelope can be reduced through validation rather than expanded later.
detailSummary:
Digital and IT’s 4 September 2026 working model materially broadens the previous four-post product-pod assumption. The mature delivery model now includes Product Manager, Product Owner, Solution Architect / Technical Lead, Backend Engineer, Full-Stack Developer, UX/UI Designer, QA engineering through Infuse, fractional Azure DevOps, a Dynamics Developer, fractional Cloud Infrastructure and fractional Cloud IAM capacity. Digital and IT’s sheet reports a gross mature-team resource cost of £56,842 per month and £682,108 over twelve months, before other costs.

For the Student Hub funding case, Mark Peace remains Product Owner from existing workload and therefore does not create an incremental cash ask. Jon Ward has also identified an IT Delivery Manager as required but expects that role to be provided from existing Digital and IT capacity; it is therefore shown as an existing dependency rather than costed new investment until Digital and IT advises otherwise. The current high-water cash baseline carries every other costed IT role at the full amount shown by Digital and IT, even where the role may ultimately be shared, supplied from existing capacity or attributable to another programme. This deliberately means carrying 100% of the Product Manager until a Staff Digital Hub allocation is agreed; a full Solution Architect / Technical Lead until the architecture model is confirmed; the listed DevOps, infrastructure and IAM fractions until Digital and IT confirms existing capacity; and the full Dynamics Developer until its actual relationship to the Student Hub, King’s Answers and wider enquiry-management work is resolved.

Using the displayed monthly role costs, the current worst-case incremental staffing envelope is £50,090 per month after removing the known existing Product Owner. For the existing November 2026 to June 2027 Year One planning period this gives £400,720; the full-year high-water run-rate is £601,080 in each subsequent year before the separate sandwich-year placement. One paid sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer remains provisioned at £35,000 in each of Years Two and Three as additional supervised developmental capacity and a talent-pipeline test, not as a substitute for experienced delivery roles.

Ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling remains a separate £90,000 annual planning allowance. James Costerton has confirmed that the Infuse line is QA/testing capacity and is not the agentic-development cost; the agentic allowance is for a dedicated Devin instance purchased from Cognition. Azure, environments and platform costs remain £50,000 in Year One. Digital and IT considers the working estimate of costs rising to around £90,000 by Year Three reasonably accurate; for the high-water envelope, £90,000 is held in both Years Two and Three until a more precise consumption profile is agreed. Year One also retains the £15,000 paid student visioning/co-design envelope under 4.1.2, while the separate 4.1.1 knowledge/content provision remains £33,000 in each mobilisation year.

On that deliberately conservative basis, the current Digital Student Experience Hub funding profile is approximately £588,720 in 2026/27, £849,080 in 2027/28 and £849,080 in 2028/29: £2,286,880 across the three-year mobilisation. This sits within the existing £3.0m strategic envelope and leaves £713,120 unallocated headroom. The purpose of the next Digital and IT conversations is to bring this high-water position down by confirming Year One phasing, existing-resource deployment, Student-versus-Staff Hub cost attribution, Dynamics scope and the sourcing model for specialist technical capacity.

The current worst-case recurrent run-rate, if every currently costed role other than Product Owner remained directly attributable to the Student Hub, is £601,080 per year for staffing and specialist capacity, plus £90,000 agentic tooling and a £90,000 Azure/platform high-water allowance: approximately £781,080 per year before any enduring knowledge/content operating model. This is a risk envelope rather than a settled BAU design and is expected to reduce as shared, existing and out-of-scope capacity is confirmed.
whatChanges: The working funding baseline moves from a four-post product pod plus light shared support to the broader Digital and IT mature-team model. The Student Hub business case now carries a high-water cash envelope for all currently costed IT roles except the known existing Product Owner, while the IT Delivery Manager and Business Analysis remain existing-capacity assumptions. The plan explicitly expects this envelope to reduce through phasing, shared-cost attribution and scope validation rather than relying on optimistic assumptions before Digital and IT confirms them.

caseForChange.opportunity: Using the current Digital and IT mature-team model as the high-water case gives the business case a defensible ceiling while preserving room to reduce the cash ask through evidence. It also makes the actual capability requirements visible: product management, architecture, engineering, design, testing, platform, identity and integration capacity can be discussed explicitly rather than being assumed to appear from shared services. The approach protects delivery confidence without prejudging which costs should ultimately sit with the Student Hub, the Staff Hub, Digital and IT business as usual or separately governed enquiry-management work.
caseForChange.intendedChange: The Hub is mobilised against a transparent mature capability model with a deliberately conservative funding envelope. Known existing roles are not rebilled; uncertain roles are funded until a credible alternative is agreed; shared institutional capacity is allocated between benefiting propositions; and roles such as the Dynamics Developer remain visible while their scope attribution is tested. Year One is then phased with Digital and IT so actual deployment can be lower than the envelope without weakening the ability to recruit or mobilise when capacity becomes necessary.
